name: Parseval/Plancherel: ||g^2||_1 = 180(zeta6-zeta7)/(pi^3 beta^7) (noise.py) and INT_0^oo u^4|ghat|^2 du = pi INT (g'')^2 = pi mu_1^4 for the clamped sampler (fewsterteo.py)

source.located: Classic theorem (Parseval 1799 for series; Plancherel 1910 for L^2(R)) -- no arXiv copy, NAMED-NOT-READ as originals. The step as the tree uses it is READ at source in C.J. Fewster, 'Lectures on quantum energy inequalities', arXiv:1208.5399v1: p.3 and p.30 (FT convention fhat(k) = INT e^{ikx} f(x) dx; 'the Fourier transform is an isomorphism of the Schwartz space to itself'); p.10 eq (1) -> eq (3) (the m = 0 Fourier bound -(1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat|^2 u^4 du becomes -(1/16 pi^2) INT_R |g''|^2 dt, i.e. exactly the one-sided Parseval step with factor pi) with the hypothesis remark p.10-11 ('remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R) ... does not apply to g with lower regularity'); p.29 eq (15) (the two-sided form (1/32 pi^3) INT_R |ghat|^2 u^4 du = (1/16 pi^2) INT |g''|^2, and '|ghat(u)|^2 is even' for real g). Clamped boundary hypothesis READ in Fewster & Teo, arXiv:gr-qc/9908073v2, Prop. 2.1 p.4 (Sobolev embedding: elements of W^{m,2}_0(I) vanish with their first m-1 derivatives on the boundary of I) and eq (1.3)/(1.5) (c_2 = 16 pi^2).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1208.5399 (pp.3,10,11,29,30) and gr-qc/9908073 (pp.1-2,4); Plancherel 1910 / Parseval 1799 NAMED-NOT-READ

published_statement: As restated at source (1208.5399 p.10, eqs (1),(3)): for m = 0, (1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat(u)|^2 u^4 du = (1/16 pi^2) INT_{-oo}^{oo} |g''(t)|^2 dt, with fhat(k) = INT e^{ikx} f(x) dx; and (p.29 eq (15)) (1/32 pi^3) INT_{-oo}^{oo} du |ghat(u)|^2 u^4 = (1/16 pi^2) INT |g''|^2, i.e. INT_R |ghat|^2 = 2 pi INT_R |g|^2 applied to g''. The theorem behind it (Plancherel, standard, not read in an original): the Fourier transform extends from L^1 cap L^2 to a bijection of L^2(R) with INT |fhat|^2 du = 2 pi INT |f|^2 dt in the e^{+-iut} convention.
published_hypotheses: f in L^2(R) (Plancherel); the restatement uses g in C_0^oo(R) for eq (1), extended by its own remark to g in W^{2,2}(R): g, g', g'' exist distributionally and are square-integrable (1208.5399 p.10)
real-valued g, so |ghat(u)|^2 is even and INT_0^oo = (1/2) INT_R (1208.5399 p.25, p.28: 'As |ghat(u)|^2 is even')

FT(g'')(u) = (-iu)^2 ghat(u) (distributional derivative): holds without boundary delta terms exactly when the zero extension is in W^{2,2}(R), i.e. g = g' = 0 at the ends of a compact support (gr-qc/9908073 Prop 2.1)
Fourier convention e^{+ikx} (1208.5399); the sign does not change |ghat|^2 for real g
hypothesis_drift: noise.py:117-118 and 581-586 (docstring) name only the series hypothesis 1/(e^x-1)^2 = SUM (n-1) e^{-nx}; the Plancherel hypotheses are UNSTATED: (i) g is the one-sided cosine transform g(u) = INT_0^oo S(k) cos(ku) dk with S = k^3 n(k)/(2 pi^2); (ii) S in L^2(0,oo); (iii) ||g^2||_1 is the WHOLE-LINE integral. All three hold here, COMPUTED (rederive A2a/A2b, A4, A6b; noise.py:650 uses Y = 2 INT_0^oo, i.e. whole line, consistent with (iii)). DROPPED-IN-STATEMENT, SATISFIED-IN-USE -- not a narrowing.
noise.py:583 series hypothesis holds only for x > 0 (0 < e^{-x} < 1); the integration range is x > 0, so it is satisfied; unstated domain, no effect (rederive A1a, A1a').

noise.py:1043 labels the check '||g^2||_1 = ..., series = closed form' and it checks ONLY the series step (SUM (n-1) 6!/n^7 /(4 pi^3) = 180(zeta6-zeta7)/pi^3); the Parseval step INT_R g^2 du = pi INT_0^oo S^2 dk is not checked there. It is exercised only indirectly by the spectral-convolution control noise.py:1048 at tau = beta (1e-8). DISCREPANCY OF COVERAGE, not an error: rederive A3 checks the Parseval step directly, position-space quadrature vs closed form, rel 2.6e-30.

fewsterteo.py:46-54, 301-303: the source's eq (1) is stated for SMOOTH compactly supported g; the clamped-beam mode is NOT C^oo on R (g'' jumps to 0 at t = 0, 1: g''(0) = g''(1) = 44.7466 after normalisation). WEAKENED regularity, licensed by the source's own W^{2,2}(R) remark (1208.5399 p.10); the zero-extended clamped mode is in W^{2,2}(R) because g = g' = 0 at both ends (rederive B1b, 3.0e-29). No narrowing.

fewsterteo.py:47-48 hypothesis 'clamped' is load-bearing and is stated and checked in the tree (fewsterteo.py:571-572); rederive B5i shows that without g' = 0 at the ends (g = sin(pi t)) the per-period integral of u^4|ghat|^2 tends to 4 pi^3 = 124.025, so INT_0^oo diverges while pi INT (g'')^2 = pi^5/2 is finite. No drift.

fewsterteo.py canonical hypothesis 'real g, integral over u >= 0' is load-bearing and stated; rederive B5ii (g e^{3it}) gives one-sided halves 7492.39 and 335.81 against pi INT|g''|^2 = 3914.13, while the two-sided sum = 2 pi INT|g''|^2 to 6.6e-6. No drift.

fewsterteo.py canonical hypothesis 'g normalised INT g^2 = 1' is NOT a Parseval hypothesis (the identity is homogeneous of degree 2); it is needed only for the last equality = pi mu_1^4. ADDED hypothesis, harmless and correct.

fewsterteo.py:306-316 _tail keeps only the period-average (g''(0)^2 + g''(1)^2)/U of the asymptotic |FT g''|^2 and drops the oscillating cross term -2 g''(0) g''(1) INT_U^oo cos(u)/u^2 du. At the tree's U = 2e4 that term is +5.83e-6 absolute = 3.70e-9 relative to pi mu_1^4; the tree's own measured residual is -3.709e-9 (quadrature + averaged tail vs pi mu^4, re-run here read-only). The residual is therefore almost entirely the dropped term, and it uses 37% of the 1e-8 tolerance at fewsterteo.py:577. RECORDED DISCREPANCY of an approximation, not an error: the check passes and the conclusion is unchanged.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (28 checks, ~2 min). (A) noise.py: sympy proves the series step (A1a-d) and that g is the one-sided cosine transform of S = k^3 n(k)/(2 pi^2) (A2a; base integral checked at u = 0.3, 1.7 to 3e-31); g(0) = pi^2/30, u^4 g -> -3/(2 pi^2) (A6); the PARSEVAL STEP ITSELF, which the tree does not check directly, by position-space quadrature of INT_R g^2 from the closed-form kernel: 0.0522114036827682170201042 = 180(zeta6-zeta7)/pi^3 to rel 2.6e-30 (A3); spectral side pi INT S^2 agrees to 3.6e-40 (A4); half-line control is half (A3-control); beta^-7 scaling (A5). (B) fewsterteo.py: mu_1 reproduced; clamping to 3e-29; INT (g'')^2 = mu^4 INT g^2 exactly (B2); INT_0^oo |FT g''|^2 = 1572.56787633412 vs pi mu^4 = 1572.56787635999, rel 1.65e-11 at U = 4000 with the exact tail incl. the oscillating cross term (B3); prefactor mu^4/(16 pi^2) = 3.169857938310468 (B4). Guards fire both ways: unclamped sampler -> divergence (B5i); complex sampler -> one-sided form fails, two-sided holds (B5ii); e^{+iut} vs e^{-iut} identical for real g (B5iii). later_literature.what: Performs the identical step: eq (1) at m = 0 -> eq (3), -(1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat|^2 u^4 = -(1/16 pi^2) INT |g''|^2, and eq (15) two-sided; states the W^{2,2}(R) regularity under which it holds and that it fails for discontinuous g; C ~ 3.17 from the clamped (g = g' = 0) eigenproblem.

Prop. 2.1: W^{m,2}_0(I) elements vanish with first m-1 derivatives on the boundary -- the clamped condition is the Sobolev-space form of 'no boundary delta terms'; c_2 = 16 pi^2 in the |D^2 g|^2 form of the massless 4D QI.

later_literature.what: Carries the Fourier-space QEI (the object the Parseval step acts on) to Moyal-deformed Minkowski space; the bound coincides with the commutative one; states sqrt(f) in H^s(R), s > 2 as a sufficient regularity condition. It does NOT itself perform or question the Parseval step. Found by the one discover_papers call; nothing found narrowing or contradicting Plancherel as used.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence is computed rather than presumed. Plancherel/Parseval is a theorem of pure analysis (Plancherel 1910): its conclusion depends on no physical measurement, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. The only numerical inputs are pi, zeta(6), zeta(7) and the root mu_1, all recomputed here to 30-40 digits (A3/A4/B1a). What a user of the theorem CAN lack is a hypothesis, not data: (i) square-integrability, (ii) real g for the one-sided factor pi, (iii) g = g' = 0 at the ends of the support for FT(g'') = -u^2 ghat. The guards show (ii) and (iii) are load-bearing -- dropping (iii) makes INT u^4|ghat|^2 diverge (B5i) and dropping (ii) moves the one-sided integral from 3914 to 7492 (B5ii) -- and the tree states and checks both. Having any later data changes nothing: the re-derivation agrees at 2.6e-30 (noise) and 1.65e-11 (fewsterteo).
grade_evidence: Statement and hypotheses as used match the restatement READ in 1208.5399 (eq (1)->(3), (15); W^{2,2} remark) and gr-qc/9908073 Prop 2.1. Re-derivation agrees: the Parseval step for the thermal kernel checked directly by position-space quadrature, INT_R g^2 = 180(zeta6-zeta7)/pi^3 to rel 2.6e-30 (the tree itself checks only the series step, noise.py:1043 -- a coverage discrepancy, recorded, not an error); the clamped-sampler identity INT_0^oo |FT g''|^2 = pi mu_1^4 to rel 1.65e-11. Every hypothesis the tree drops from its statement (noise.py: cosine-transform representation, L^2, whole-line norm, x > 0) is satisfied in its use, computed. The load-bearing hypotheses (clamping, real g) are stated in fewsterteo.py and their removal is shown to break the identity (guards fire). No measured datum enters. One recorded discrepancy of approximation: fewsterteo._tail drops an oscillating cross term worth 3.70e-9 relative at U = 2e4, which accounts for the tree's -3.709e-9 residual inside its 1e-8 tolerance; conclusion unchanged.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if a tree site applied the one-sided form 'INT_0^oo u^4|ghat|^2 = pi INT (g'')^2' to a complex or non-clamped sampler (none found at the owner sites: noise.py:117-118, 581-586, 1043; fewsterteo.py:46-54, 301-303, 575-580), or if ||g^2||_1 were used as a half-line integral somewhere (noise.py:650 uses the whole line). A tightening of fewsterteo.py:577's tolerance below ~4e-9 without adding the cross term would make that check FAIL (a check fault, not a fault of Parseval). WRONG only on a computed counterexample to the equalities, which the quadratures above exclude to 1e-11 and 1e-30.
